cues: A cook dices ripe produce into chilled fruit salad, balancing soft pieces with tart, juicy chunks.
Blending tropical fruit with yogurt makes a thick breakfast drink, especially when chilled pieces soften during mixing.
A vendor trims tough outer layers before portioning sweet flesh for skewers at an outdoor market.
Chunks fold into sweet-and-sour dishes, where heat caramelizes sugars and bright acidity balances savory sauces.
A baker folds chopped fruit into quick-bread batter, where oven heat softens pieces and browns their sugars.
Cooks grill thick fruit slices until sugars char and the edges develop smoky sweetness.
Peeling fruit over a compost pail keeps sticky scraps off the counter before its flesh is sliced.
Cut tropical fruit can be chilled in sealed containers, slowing discoloration while preserving its aroma for later snacking.
